scenes.title: Participant wired to palm skin-conductance sensors hesitating over rigged Deck B vs vmPFC flatline on the four-deck Iowa Gambling table
scenes.era: 1994-1996, University of Iowa Department of Neurology testing suite, Iowa City

layout.description: Sunlit 1994 Iowa clinical neuropsychology room with a green-baize tabletop holding four neat face-down card decks labeled 'A', 'B', 'C', and 'D', two small fingertip skin-conductance sensors taped to the non-drawing palm, and a dual-channel polygraph monitor.

positions.who: Healthy Participant / Patient comparison mannequin (in 1994 collared sweater)
positions.where: seated at the four-deck table with right hand hovering two inches above high-risk Deck B — then pulling back smoothly to draw from safe Deck D as the palm sensor trace spikes
positions.facing: facing Decks A, B, C, D

positions.who: Antonio Damasio & Antoine Bechara (mannequins in tailored suit and white clinical coat)
positions.where: standing beside the polygraph monitor pointing to the sharp 5-second 'Pre-Deck-B Warning Spike' versus Patient Elliot's dead-flat pre-draw line

props.name: four labeled card decks ('A', 'B' trap decks vs 'C', 'D' steady decks)
props.period_detail: four crisp white card stacks where flipped Deck B card reveals '+100 / PENALTY -1250'
props.physical_behavior: visualizes immediate lure vs long-term ruin

props.name: fingertip galvanic skin-conductance leads
props.period_detail: two clean silver sensor clips on left index and middle fingers wired to the polygraph

props.name: split polygraph trace ('Healthy Pre-Reach Warning Spike' vs 'vmPFC Flat Pre-Reach')
props.period_detail: large clean monitor comparing a sharp warning peak before Deck B against a flat horizontal line

actions.verb_sequence: starts reaching toward flashy Deck B -> 5-second palm conductance spike leaps up on the monitor -> hand pivots smoothly across to draw from safe Deck D
contrasts that anticipatory spike against Patient Elliot's flat pre-draw trace despite intact 97th-percentile IQ folder

reactions.reaction: taps the 'IQ: Superior / Real-Life Choice: Impaired' clinical chart, overturning Descartes
stacks steady net winnings beside Decks C and D

scenes.wardrobe: 1994 Iowa neurology attire: Damasio in classic dark tailored European suit and tie; Bechara in crisp white physician coat; participant in knit sweater.
scenes.lighting: Clean high-key clinical daylight across four crisp card decks and monitor.
scenes.recognition_hook: Five seconds before a healthy player's fingers even touch rigged Deck B, palm sensors fire a warning spike — erase that emotional circuit, and a 97th-percentile genius goes broke.

key_visual.description: a 1994 neurology test table with four card decks labeled A, B, C, D and fingertip skin-conductance leads beside a monitor showing a pre-reach warning spike

scenes.title: Patient Elliot paralyzed for 30 minutes choosing between two Tuesday appointment slots

layout.description: Sunlit doctor's desk covered in six pages of neat handwritten pros-and-cons weather/traffic calculations just to pick 'Tuesday 1:30 vs Wednesday 2:00'.

positions.where: calmly filling page six of pros-and-cons for a trivial calendar slot with zero emotional tie-breaker

props.name: six pages of endless pros-and-cons notes & desk calendar
props.physical_behavior: shows pure reason without somatic weights spinning forever

actions.verb_sequence: weighs Tuesday afternoon sunlight vs Wednesday parking endlessly -> Antonio Damasio gently says 'Let's do Tuesday' -> Elliot calmly says 'Fine' and closes book

reactions.reaction: realizes emotion isn't reason's enemy — it's reason's tie-breaker

scenes.recognition_hook: With a 97th-percentile IQ and zero emotional tags, Elliot spent half an hour unable to pick a Tuesday appointment slot.

scenes.title: Knowing vs Feeling: Saying 'Deck B is bad' while still drawing Deck B

layout.description: Close view of the four card decks at Card #80.

positions.where: pointing verbally to 'C & D = Good' on a question sheet, then immediately reaching right back onto Bad Deck B

props.name: flat pre-draw polygraph line at Card 80
props.period_detail: zero visceral deterrent despite intact verbal knowledge

actions.verb_sequence: states aloud 'A and B lose' -> reaches onto Deck B anyway as palm line stays flat

scenes.recognition_hook: Saying 'that deck is a trap' out loud didn't stop the hand when the brain's somatic warning bridge was offline.

scenes.title: Separating real experienced gut alarms from trivial 'toaster paralysis'

layout.description: Bright desk where a shopper closes 15 identical appliance review tabs with a 2-minute timer while pausing seriously on a major contract red flag.

positions.where: closing 15 trivial comparison tabs briskly, then circling a risky penalty clause in a contract carefully

props.name: 2-minute tie-breaker timer & contract highlight
props.period_detail: smart pairing of data + somatic experience

actions.verb_sequence: caps trivial tie choice in 2 minutes -> inspects real high-stakes penalty clause thoroughly

scenes.recognition_hook: Cap equal-value minor choices at two minutes — and when experienced intuition flags a 'Deck B' contract, read the fine print twice.
